design_decisions: Peer completion latches the backend's settled state but never stops a post-game watch the frontend still owns. The backend must keep publishing advancing timestamps so the frontend can form its three-sample distinct-timestamp quorum.

The frontend publishes SYNCTHING COMPLETE and then calls stopWatch. In normal mode that release stops the watcher; debug extended observation is allowed only after manager release, and then ends when all peers finish or an existing terminal boundary is reached.
A stopped but registered watcher freezes latest_sample, and manager polling honestly returns that frozen sample. The bug was stopping too early, not poll_watch() returning the last known sample.

No README.md edit is needed: the user-facing definition of SYNCTHING COMPLETE remains that the local folder has settled and one connected peer has confirmed content receipt; only stop ownership changed.

review_history: Four consecutive defects on the predecessor branch shared the wrong-test-shape pattern: watch-level tests exercised a sequence the running system never performs and could not see the frontend quorum. Task 2's manager-poll harness closes that gap by reproducing the observed polling sequence rather than reading watch.latest_sample directly.
Review 01 accepted Task 1 after verifying the explicit released-state guard, the separation of latching from stopping, and mutations that failed in both normal and debug modes.
Review 02 accepted Task 2 after verifying the harness polls through SyncthingWatchManager.poll_watch() and demonstrably catches the original frozen-timestamp regression.

deferred_verification: A post-game Steam Deck run is required before this is considered fixed. The expected signature is SYNCTHING COMPLETE within roughly twenty seconds of handoff while a transition still reports non-zero needed_deletes, with no LOCAL BACKUP SAVED - SYNCTHING UPLOAD INCOMPLETE at the 300-second mark.
Debug extended observation has no device evidence after this fix and must be treated as a first hardware test, not a re-confirmation.

The unchanged 90-second stall window, 900-second backend hard ceiling, and 300-second frontend no-evidence ceiling remain unexercised. The captured 2026-08-11 failure proves only that the frontend ceiling fires as designed after a backend-side premature stop.
The accepted stop_watch() race from the predecessor branch is unchanged by this plan.
